Hi all — ran a conservative sizing exercise. I kept the math explicit so you can tweak assumptions. High level summary first, details below:

Recommendation (pilot): reserve 6 x A100-80GB GPUs in a Dedicated pool, with autoscaling to +2 GPUs for burst. Use int8 quant (weight compression + kernel support) for production if quality is acceptable; use fp16 for baseline dev/testing.

Why 6 GPUs: with int8 and batching tuned we can sustain ~14–18 effective RPS per GPU for the Lumen-34B inference profile at 1.2k tokens avg; at 12 RPS steady this gives ~20–25% headroom and room for 20 RPS short bursts with autoscale. If you insist on fp16-only, plan ~10 GPUs.

Sizing details (approx):
- Model weights (inference residency):
  - Lumen-34B fp16: ~68 GB total weights (naive); fp16 footprint requires multi-GPU sharding — safe to assume ~1.5x replication + optimizer-free runtime overlay; practical per-GPU residency on 80GB devices is tight for fp16 without model parallelism.
  - Lumen-34B int8 (stable kernels): ~20–24 GB effective weights per GPU (post quant/sharding) — much friendlier for single-node serving and KV cache headroom.
  - Lumen-34B int4 (experimental): ~12–14 GB weights but with more kernel/quality caveats.

- KV cache memory (dominant with long context):
  - KV per token estimate: ~250 bytes/token (including keys+values, attention buffers, and runtime overhead). This is conservative to cover sharded KV layouts and library overhead.
  - For 32k context: 32,000 * 250 B ≈ 8,000,000 B ≈ 8.0 GB of KV storage per request (per sequence) stored in GPU memory (can be sharded across GPUs in the pod).
  - For active batching and multiple concurrent requests, you won't keep full 32k KV per concurrent request if prefix caching is used — prefix caching reduces duplicated KV for repeated prefixes across calls.

- Working memory / activations: assume additional 6–10 GB per GPU depending on sequence lengths and beam/search settings.

Putting it together (per-GPU usable memory math, rough):
- With int8 weights (~22 GB) + KV shard for 32k (~8 GB) + activations (~8 GB) + OS/runtime (~4 GB) = ~42 GB used on a GPU. On an 80 GB A100 that leaves ~38 GB headroom for batching and additional shards.
- With fp16 weights (~68 GB spread across GPUs) you'd need more GPUs to shard weights (hence the recommendation of ~10 GPUs for fp16 mode).

Concurrency math (quick):
- Observed throughput (int8, tuned kernels): ~15 RPS/GPU @ ~1.2k avg tokens.
- For 12 steady RPS -> 12 / 15 ≈ 0.8 GPUs needed (but we allocate whole GPUs). Accounting for batching inefficiencies, tail SLOs, and replication for redundancy, we recommend 6 GPUs for the pool to cover multi-tenant overhead (routing/resilience in Dedicated) and burst headroom to 20 RPS with autoscale +2.

Operational notes / options:
- KV caching strategy: enable prefix-level persistent KV for repeated patient records. This reduces effective KV memory footprint across requests and greatly improves latency/cost.
- Sharding policy: colocate complete KV shard + local weight shard where possible — avoids cross-GPU KV fetch latency.
- Fallbacks: keep an int8 model variant as fallback for overloaded regions; automatic downgrade policy in Redwood can switch traffic to int8 if capacity constrained.

Caveats: numbers above are conservative but not bench-verified on a customer checkpoint. If you can share a small sample model/init or let us run a 1-GPU perf test, we can tighten the estimate.

Next steps:
1) Confirm willingness to run int8 candidate for quality check.
2) If yes, we provision 6xA100-80GB reserved + autoscale 2 for pilot. Lead time: 10–14 business days for Dedicated reserved pool provisioning in us-west.

Happy to jump on a short call to step through the math.

— Aditya
